title: A gap between clips closes with a click and Delete
goal: Lifting a stretch out with semicolon, or dragging a clip away, leaves an empty gap on the track, and the only way to close it is to drag a range over it and press Shift Delete. In Premiere and Final Cut you click the gap and press Delete, or right-click it and choose Ripple Delete. Make a gap something you can click and close the same way.
notes: From the manager pass's Premiere gap check 2026-10-07. Today: no gap-picking concept; closeGap is private in Sources/PhotonzCore/TimelineMenuEdits.swift ~41-56 and used only by ripple delete of a clip. A drag on empty track space draws a box (TrackRange). Lift is ; (TimelineKeys.swift ~231-237). Core first (TDD): a TimelineGap value (track, startMS, lengthMS) found from the track's clips at a time, and a closeGap edit that moves later clips, their linked sound and their captions, refusing when it would overlap. The click and its picked tint live in the timeline view; reuse the ruler/track range tint, add no new style, and add Ripple Delete to the gap's right-click menu per the 'Actions live where you click' rule. Placement: right-click row on the thing it acts on, plus the existing Sequence > Ripple Delete row; no new control. Searched pick a gap, close gap, ripple delete a gap (--all): nothing covers it, and no card declined it.
acceptance: Clicking the empty stretch between two clips on a track picks that gap, drawn with the same picked tint the app already uses for a picked time range, and a click anywhere else lets it go

With a gap picked, Delete, Shift Delete and the Sequence menu's Ripple Delete close it: everything after it on that track moves earlier by the gap's length, together with its own sound and its captions, in one undo step

Right-clicking a gap opens a menu whose first row is Ripple Delete, and it is dimmed when closing the gap would push a clip into another (a locked track, or a later clip on a track that moves with it)
A drag that starts in empty track space still draws a box as today, and a click on empty space after the last clip picks nothing

Try path at Next defaults: open the talk sample, cut twice with Command K, press semicolon on the middle piece, click the gap, press Delete. A walk does this and checks the pieces and the captions; audit written under queue/audits/. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: adversarial review: a Premiere editor clicks a gap and presses Delete, or right-clicks it for Ripple Delete; both now work. A SwiftUI context menu cannot see where it was opened, so each gap gets its own hit area on the lane carrying the same press gesture (read in the lane's coordinate space) and its own menu. Captions are standalone layers, so 'its captions' = caption lines starting over a clip that moves. Captions-track spaces are pauses, not gaps: no gap picking there. The mock (video-cut-wt step 7) draws an unpicked gap dashed and hatched; the app draws bare lane: filed a-gap-on-a-track-looks-like-an-empty-slot-dashed.

built: PhotonzCore/TimelineGap.swift (TimelineGap, gap(onTrack:atMS:), gaps(onTrack:), canCloseGap, closeGap; refuses on a locked layer or track, or any landing overlap), 12 tests in TimelineGapTests. App: EditorState+TimelineGap.swift; a click in a gap picks it (EditorState+TrackRange); Delete, Shift Delete, Sequence Ripple Delete and Edit 'Delete Gap' close it; the picked gap is drawn with the track-range band (TimelineDock); the gap's right-click menu leads with Ripple Delete (TimelineTrackRows). Harness: a picked gap reads as 'Gap on <track>' in expectTimelinePick; new action captionsExpectOverClips.

verified: Scripts/test.sh 11777 tests green; a-gap-between-clips-closes-walk green at Next defaults (Delete, Shift Delete and right-click Ripple Delete each close the 4.0-8.0s gap, tail lands 4.00-13.25, every caption over a clip); marquee-and-track-range, extract-a-marked-stretch and draw-a-range-on-the-ruler walks green.

left rough (not filed): a lifted clip's second half is named '<name> copy' (Lift's naming, not this task); a refused close only beeps; only the gap's own track ripples, so titles and music elsewhere stay (Premiere with sync lock off).
